entities.summary: Quintus Fabius Ambustus Vibulanus, a member of the esteemed gens Fabia, played a pivotal role in ancient Rome's early history. The Fabii family's illustrious career spanned over two centuries, with three brothers serving as consul simultaneously in 485-479 BC, solidifying their reputation. The Fabii's most notable achievement was their bravery during the Battle of Cremera in 477 BC, where 306 Fabii fought against the Gauls. Their sacrifice cemented the family's legacy, and they would go on to claim 45 consulships throughout the Republic. The Fabii's influence extended beyond their own family, shaping the course of Roman politics and culture. The Battle of Cremera, in particular, marked a turning point in Roman history, as it showcased the Fabii's military prowess and paved the way for future Roman conquests. The Fabii's legacy can be seen in the many Roman institutions and monuments they helped establish, including the construction of the Via Appia, a major road that connected Rome to the surrounding regions. The Fabii's impact on Roman society was profound, and their name became synonymous with bravery and patriotism. Quintus Fabius Ambustus Vibulanus's contributions to Roman history are a testament to the enduring power of the gens Fabia.
